gaps.title: Leave request submission content and rules are undefined and the New request page was not captured
gaps.description: What an employee enters when submitting a leave request (leave type, start and end dates, partial days, reason, attachments) and which rules apply (balance limits, overlapping requests, notice period) are not defined. The decision recorded against this question (DEC-001) talks about rejection reasons and resubmission and does not address submission data. The New request link's target failed to capture (HTTP 404), so no form, fields or validation are shown in the capture.

evidence_refs.locator: SCR-011 fields (type, duration in days, status only)

gaps.why_it_matters: Submitting a request is the entry point of the whole leave workflow; the list only shows a type and a whole-day duration, so the data model for dates, partial days and balance cannot be derived from the mockup.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The submission form, its validation and the stored request data cannot be specified; employees could submit requests that exceed balance or overlap without anyone deciding whether that is allowed.
research_questions: Which fields do established HR leave-management products (for example BambooHR, Personio, Workday) collect on a leave request, including partial-day and date-range handling?
How do leave-management products typically handle a request that exceeds the remaining leave balance or overlaps an existing request (block, warn, or allow)?

gaps.title: Conditions for the manager's-manager fallback approver are undefined
gaps.description: DEC-002 states that managers decide only for their direct reports and that the manager's own manager can act when the manager is away. How 'away' is determined, whether the fallback approver can act at any time or only during the absence, what happens when the fallback approver is also away or the manager has no manager, and who decides on a manager's own leave request are not defined.
gaps.why_it_matters: Approval has payroll and legal effect (CQ-002); the permission check for Approve and Reject depends on knowing exactly when a second-level manager is entitled to act.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Either the fallback approver can act whenever they like, undermining the direct-reports-only rule, or requests stall when the direct manager is absent; requests from top-level managers may have no valid approver.
research_questions: How do HR systems commonly model approval delegation or escalation when the approving manager is absent (out-of-office flag, explicit delegate, time-based escalation)?

gaps.title: Entering a rejection reason and the correct-and-resubmit flow are not shown in the capture
gaps.description: Decisions state that a reason is required when rejecting, the employee sees it, and a rejected request can be corrected and resubmitted. The captured request page shows only Approve and Reject buttons with no reason input, and no rejected-request or resubmission screen was captured. What can be changed on resubmission, whether it returns to the same approver, and how the earlier rejection and its reason relate to the resubmitted request are not defined.
gaps.why_it_matters: The rejection reason is a confirmed must-have that the employee relies on to correct the request; without a defined resubmission flow the Rejected state is a dead end for the employee.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Rejections could be recorded without a reason, and the resubmission behaviour (new request vs same request, history, approver) would be invented during build.

gaps.title: Full status model and the view of decided requests are undefined
gaps.description: Only Pending and Approved are shown; decisions imply a Rejected status and a resubmitted state. Whether other statuses exist (for example cancelled or withdrawn), and what the detail page shows for a decided request, are unknown. The Approved request's detail page failed to capture (HTTP 404), so whether Approve and Reject remain visible on decided requests is not shown in the capture.
gaps.why_it_matters: REQ-003 promises employees can see the status of each request, so every status and its meaning must be known; the decided-request view is where the employee sees the rejection reason.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Status values and allowed transitions are undefined, and managers might be offered Approve or Reject on requests already decided.

gaps.title: Which requests each role sees in the list is undefined
gaps.description: The list shows two requests without indicating whose they are. Whether an employee sees only their own requests, whether a manager sees direct reports' requests in the same list or elsewhere, and whether the fallback approver sees their indirect reports' requests are not defined. Whether the deciding manager is visible to the employee is also open.
gaps.why_it_matters: Leave requests include sick leave and rejection reasons about named employees; showing requests beyond the viewer's own or their reports' exposes personal data to colleagues.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The list query and access checks cannot be specified; employees could see colleagues' leave, or managers could miss requests awaiting their decision.

gaps.title: Confirmation and reversal of Approve and Reject are undefined
gaps.description: Whether Approve or Reject asks for confirmation, and whether a decision can be changed or reversed afterwards (for example approved leave later revoked), are not defined. The capture shows no confirmation step. Decisions cover only resubmission after rejection, not reversal by the manager.
gaps.why_it_matters: Approve and Reject sit side by side as single-click buttons; a mis-click affects an employee's leave and payroll, and an approved absence may already be planned around.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Mistaken decisions may be unrecoverable, or reversible without any record or rule about who may reverse them.
research_questions: What confirmation and undo patterns do established approval workflows use for single-click approve/reject actions with downstream payroll effect?

gaps.title: Two approvers acting on the same request at once is unhandled
gaps.description: With the fallback rule in DEC-002, both a manager and that manager's manager can be entitled to decide the same request. What happens when both act at nearly the same time, when a stale page shows a request as Pending after it was decided, or when a button is clicked twice, is not defined.
gaps.why_it_matters: One approval is enough, so the first decision is final; two people with rights on the same request make conflicting approve and reject outcomes possible.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: A request could be both approved and rejected, or the last click could silently overwrite the first decision and its effects.
research_questions: What are established patterns for preventing conflicting or duplicate state transitions on a single record when two authorised users act concurrently (for example optimistic concurrency with version checks)?
How should a web UI inform a user that the record they are acting on was already decided by someone else?

gaps.title: Who is notified of submissions and decisions is undefined
gaps.description: Whether managers are told about new requests, whether employees are told about approvals or rejections (including the rejection reason), whether the fallback manager is told when a request awaits them, through which channel, and what happens if delivery fails are not defined. The notification part of CQ-003 has no recorded answer.
gaps.why_it_matters: Employees must act on rejections (correct and resubmit) and the fallback approval only works if the second-level manager knows a request is waiting.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Requests may sit pending unnoticed and employees may not learn of rejections in time to resubmit before their planned leave.

gaps.title: Downstream effects of an approval (leave balance, payroll) are undefined
gaps.description: What changes when a request is approved or rejected, such as deduction from a leave balance or a hand-off to payroll, and what happens to those effects if a decision is reversed or a request resubmitted, are not defined.
gaps.why_it_matters: An approval is the point at which leave becomes an entitlement used; if balances exist, approve, reject, reversal and resubmission must keep them consistent.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Balances could be double-deducted on resubmission or left wrong after reversals, with payroll consequences.

gaps.title: Handling of sick-leave and rejection-reason data as personal data is undefined
gaps.description: The list shows a Sick leave request and the feature stores free-text rejection reasons about named employees. Who may see the leave type, what reason text may contain, and how long such records are kept are not defined.
gaps.why_it_matters: Sick leave can reveal health information about an employee, which privacy law in many jurisdictions treats as a special category with stricter handling than ordinary leave.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Health-related information could be shown or retained more widely or longer than permitted.
research_questions: Under GDPR Article 9, is the fact that an employee took sick leave treated as health data, and what does that imply for who may see it in an HR leave system?
What retention periods are typical or required for employee leave and absence records?

gaps.title: Record of who decided each request and when is undefined
gaps.description: Whether each approval, rejection, reversal and resubmission must be recorded with who acted, in what capacity (direct manager or fallback manager), and when, is not defined, nor whether the employee can see who decided.
gaps.why_it_matters: Because a second-level manager can decide on behalf of an absent manager, disputes about a decision need to show who actually decided and under which rule.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Decisions with payroll effect could not be traced or disputed reliably.

gaps.title: Empty, loading, success and error states are not shown in the capture
gaps.description: The list shows only a populated default state and the request page only an enabled Pending state. No empty list, loading, post-decision success or failure state is shown in the capture.
gaps.checklist_item: Empty, loading, success and error states
gaps.why_it_matters: A new employee starts with no requests, and a manager needs to know whether an approval actually succeeded before telling the employee.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: These states will be designed ad hoc, and a failed decision may look like a successful one.

gaps.title: Accessibility of status display and decision feedback is undefined
gaps.description: How request status and the outcome of Approve or Reject are conveyed to assistive technology users, and how a required rejection reason is labelled and its errors announced, are not defined.
gaps.why_it_matters: Status visibility is a core requirement and the decision result appears without a page change; a required reason field adds validation messages that must be perceivable.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Screen-reader users may not learn whether a decision succeeded or why a rejection was blocked.
research_questions: What do WCAG 2.2 success criteria 4.1.3 (Status Messages) and 3.3.1/3.3.2 (Error Identification, Labels or Instructions) require for an approve/reject action with a required reason field?

assumptions.text: DEC-001's verbatim answer does not address CQ-001 (submission data and rules), so the submission content is treated as still open.
assumptions.why: DEC-001 was matched to CQ-001 by keywords and its text concerns rejection reasons and resubmission.
assumptions.impact: GAP-001 is raised despite REQ-001 being approved with its unknown issue cleared.
assumptions.to_confirm: Confirm with the customer what a leave request contains and which submission rules apply.

assumptions.text: DEC-001 and DEC-003 are taken as answering that a rejection reason is required and shown to the employee and that rejected requests can be resubmitted; the reversal and notification parts of CQ-003 are treated as unanswered.
assumptions.why: The verbatim text covers only rejection reasons and resubmission.
assumptions.impact: No gap is raised for whether a reason is required; GAP-006 and GAP-008 remain open.
assumptions.to_confirm: Confirm whether decisions can be reversed and who is notified.

assumptions.text: The captured Leave requests screen is assumed to be shown to both employees and managers, because the capture does not indicate the viewer's role.
assumptions.why: The same screen links to New request (an employee action) and to a page with Approve and Reject (a manager action).
assumptions.impact: GAP-005 treats list visibility per role as open.
assumptions.to_confirm: Confirm whether employees and managers have separate views.

proposed_status_changes.reason: DEC-001 does not answer CQ-001: the data a leave request contains and the submission rules are still not stated, and the New request page failed to capture.
